narrative.overview:
Redlin's visual system is a learning science laboratory where intelligence is being forged — not a sanitized dashboard that tracks it. It lives in deep, calm surfaces (navy #1A2A3A, near-black #07141f, light gray #F5F7FA) sliced open by the teal-to-purple gradient that is the product's brand signature. Teal (#20C997) is the dominant voice — it signals action, progress, correctness, and mastery. Purple (#7F63F4) joins it as an equal partner in the gradient, and stands alone as a secondary accent in the study interface. The warm coral (#FF7E67) and amber (#FFB400) provide contrast and warmth in a system that would otherwise read as purely tech-forward.

The system operates across two visual registers that share one palette and one motion identity:

1. **The Landing (Persuade):** a cinematic, motion-driven, semi-dark surface with hero gradient, floating blobs, and GSAP-staggered hero text. Deep navy background, frosted-glass navbar (backdrop-blur), and bold teal-purple accents fill the viewport.
2. **The App Shell (Operate):** a light-gray ground (#e9e9e9) with a dark-themed sidebar, light study cards, and teal-purple accents. Sharper, quieter, no radial gradients — the intelligence shows its work through clean structure and precise color rather than spectacle.

The motion identity is a settled fact: GSAP + Lenis smooth scroll, the WavyBackground ribbon, canvas-confetti on success milestones, and audio cues (button click, card flip, drop card, UI pop) give every interaction physical presence.

This system actively rejects three aesthetics: no clinical flat-minimal science-tool corporate, no childish gamification (bright candy colors and cartoon hue), and no generic dark-mode-default (the same dark floor). The anti-reference is: not an AI tool that looks like all the other AI tools.
keyCharacteristics: Teal-first: #20C997 owns the most surface presence — landing CTA, primary app button, selected state, mastery marker, XP indicator.
Dark + light hybrid: the landing lives on deep navy; the app shell on light gray. Both pull from the same palette family.
Gradient as signature: the 135deg teal→purple gradient is the brand symbol — deployed at hero CTA, logo mark, progress bar, mastery milestone, but NEVER as a background wash.
Colored shadows: shadows are sparse here but they glow — teal glow shadows on landing hero buttons and card groups. Every shadow is deliberate, not ambient elevation.
Motion is the continuum: Lenis smooth scroll, GSAP text animation, canvas-confetti on mastery — these are qualities of the identity, not decoration.
Sound presence: four cue mp3s (button click, card flip, drop, pop) + the WavyBackground's canvas wave. Removing sound removes 30% of the system's immediate character.

rules.name: The Teal Reserve Rule
rules.body: Every screen in the product must carry at least one teal or purple accent element — a button, a marker, a badge, an icon, a divider. An entirely neutral screen should not exist in the codebase.

rules.name: The Gradient Moderation Rule
rules.body: The 135deg teal→purple gradient is used in only three places: the landing hero CTA button, the logo mark, and the mastery-accomplishment badge. Its rarity is the point — never used as a background wash.

rules.name: The Two-Register Separation Rule
rules.body: Landing surfaces use navy, gradient, glow. App (dashboard) surfaces use light gray + solid teal or purple — never the gradient. No app surface should contain a rotational or horizontal teal-to-purple gradient container.

dos: Do use the teal→purple gradient only on the landing and on hero/milestone moments in the app — never as a full-container fill.
Do carry teal or purple as an enduring accent on every screen in the product — boxes, active states, progress indicators.
Do keep the two visual registers cleanly separate: the landing uses dark navy + gradient + backdrop-shader; the app uses light gray + solid teal/purple.
Do animate with attention and precision — GSAP or using CSS transitions for all interactive state changes and appearances.
Do use the color confetti explosion on success/milestone moments to make the loop feel earned and rewarded.
donts: Do not ever use a flat zero-shadow, zero-radius 'sanitized lab' look anywhere. This system has, can, and will be actively rejects that.
Do not insert the gradient into the static in-app pages' solid main content area — the text is not allowed; it is: for hero pom-only.
Do not mix the two registers inside the product — landing colors do not belong in the app shell, and the app-shell gray is not used on the landing.
Do not remove the frosted-glass blur effect from the landing navbar; it's a characteristic stroke of dark brand identity.
Do not ship screens that lack a motion identity — even if the screen is static, its hover/transition/tab/expand should carry the motion signature.
Do not introduce a fresh high-frequency color to the palette without code-safe review — the teal/purple/slate family is the ceiling.
